subject: Private Offer: net revenue allocation & reseller fees for Acme PO
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cloudreseller.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplaceops@cloudreseller.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer request — Acme PO and reseller fee mechanics

Ben —

Thanks for taking this. Acme Analytics (our customer) wants to accept the private offer but procurement has two outstanding items before they can issue the PO: 1) clarity on how Redwood calculates "net revenue" when marketplace passbacks / reseller fees are applied, and 2) an explicit line-item treatment for brokerage/transaction fees (their procurement requires an itemized breakdown).

We attached Acme's PO template and our initial notes. Questions from our side:
- Do you treat reseller passbacks as a discount off list (i.e., gross -> list price less passback = net), or do you treat them as a contra-revenue after gross is recorded?
- Can Redwood accept a 7.5% reseller passback to CloudReseller Co. and a separate 1.5% brokerage fee (both deducted from list price) while still honoring the proposed committed unit price?
- For multi-tier commits (0-100k, 100k-300k, >300k), do you prefer list-price buckets or effective net buckets for triggering tiers?

Timeline: Acme is pushing for a DocuSign package this week (they said by Friday). Can you confirm mechanics and send a proposed price matrix we can attach to the private offer?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Tom Reynolds
Head of Partnerships, CloudReseller Co.
marketplaceops@cloudreseller.com

Tom — looping in Marissa (RevOps/channel) and Aditya (Legal) to confirm the accounting/treatment and whether we can accept the two-tier passback + brokerage structure. Quick answers below and attached is a proposed price matrix with three buckets (see RDW_proposed_price_matrix_3Tiers.xlsx).

High-level options (pick one):
1) List-price carveout (preferred): treat reseller passbacks and brokerage fees as discounts off list before calculating committed thresholds. This keeps invoiced unit price aligned with the private offer and is easiest operationally.
2) Contra-revenue post-booking: Redwood books gross and records reseller passback as a contra-revenue line — acceptable but complicates reporting for the customer and may affect committed threshold calculation.

Our recommendation: option 1. With that approach we can accommodate a 7.5% reseller passback + 1.5% brokerage fee within the current committed pricing if you accept a small floor on the net effective price for the lowest tier.

Threshold mechanics: we prefer list-price buckets (that is, commits measured at list before passbacks) to avoid disputes about tier-walking when marketplace passbacks are applied after the fact. If Acme insists on net buckets, we need explicit weekly reporting and reconciliation language.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa: please confirm channel waterflow (passback -> RDW credit or marketplace refund) and margin waterfall language for the PO appendix.
- Aditya: please confirm legal redline for the passback being treated as a discount; flag anything that would require accounting changes.

Tom, I attached the price matrix with the minor floor adjustment called out in the notes. If that looks OK we can produce a DocuSign private offer and prefill with the acceptances.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: RDW_proposed_price_matrix_3Tiers.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer request — Acme PO and reseller fee mechanics

Ben / Tom —

Thanks for the clear framing. Confirming Redwood's preferred channel margin waterfall (we recommend this wording for the PO appendix):

- Step 1: List price (published RDW SKU price)
- Step 2: Marketplace/reseller passback (deducted from list as an explicit discount line item)
- Step 3: Brokerage/transaction fee (separate discount line item; shown after passback)
- Step 4: Net payable to Redwood (invoiced amount)

Why this order: keeps list-based commit math clean, marketplace reporting simple, and avoids retroactive disputes about tier attainment. We are OK with a combined 9% deduction (7.5% passback + 1.5% brokerage) treated as discounts; we ask that the private offer include the exact %s and that the DocuSign annex include a short reconciliation clause: "Marketplace will provide monthly reconciliation to confirm passbacks and tiers; disputes escalated within 30 days."

On tiers: we prefer list-price buckets. If Acme requires net-bucket measurement we require weekly reporting from CloudReseller and a 45-day reconciliation window in the PO.

Operational asks before DocuSign:
- Confirm Acme's legal name on the PO (Procurement Acme — please confirm legal entity)
- Confirm billing contact and tax treatment (VAT/US sales tax)
- Provide the exact passback %s in the RDW matrix (Tom, you already suggested 7.5% + 1.5%)

If we get agreement by EOD Thursday we can publish the private offer and route for signatures to meet Acme's Friday ask.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
